position: Office of Air and Radiation: Policy-Specific Actions, National Ambient Air Quality Standards
proposal: The Mandate recommends reviewing Biden-era interstate pollution transport regulations so that they do not require more reductions from upwind states than the statute allows, as the Supreme Court has construed it. It also recommends reversing the 2022 expansion of the Good Neighbor program beyond power plants, and limiting section 126(b) petitions to a reasonably discrete group of upwind sources.

status_summary: The federal Good Neighbor Plan for the 2015 ozone standard, which extended nitrogen oxide limits to industrial sources beyond power plants, has been stayed since 2024 through court stays, including the Supreme Court's June 2024 stay, and an EPA administrative stay issued 2024-10-29. EPA's program page says that in March 2025 EPA announced it would reconsider the plan. On 2026-01-30 EPA published a proposal to approve interstate transport plans from eight states for the 2015 ozone standard; it states that, if finalized, EPA would no longer be able or willing to lift the stay for states with approved plans, and that EPA intends to address the Good Neighbor Plan and remaining states in a future action. EPA's program page calls the proposal the first step in reconsidering the plan. The comment period was extended to 2026-03-23. Federal Register searches through 2026-10-13 found no final action on the proposal and no proposal to repeal the plan.

timeline.event: EPA announced plans to work with states on their plans and to reconsider the Good Neighbor Plan, according to its program page.

EPA published a proposal to approve eight states' 2015 ozone interstate transport plans, stating it would not lift the stay of the federal plan for states with approved plans and would address the plan itself in a later action.
EPA extended the comment period on the proposal to 2026-03-23.
